title: Heterogeneous GPU stressbench suite for distributed TP/PP throughput and regression gating
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal:
Build a reproducible stress/throughput benchmark suite that exercises multi-GPU, multi-node inference topologies (both tensor and pipeline parallel combinations) across heterogeneous GPU pools. The suite must measure tokens/sec, steady-state throughput, p95 token latency, and provide automated regression detection that can be used as a CI gate for runtime changes.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: cross-node TP/PP topologies, mixed GPU types (A100, H100, 80GB/40GB), variable microbatch sizes, KV cache warm/cold, prefix caching behavior, and sequence length sweeps (128/512/2048). Include end-to-end harness that drives the runtime over gRPC/REST and records both client-side and server-side metrics.
- Non-goal: full model quality evaluation (LLM output correctness), exhaustive model zoo coverage on first iteration. Focus on representative model sizes (7B, 34B, 70B) and one quantized variant per size.

Requirements:
1) Deterministic workloads: scripted prompts and deterministic rng seeds where applicable to reduce noise.
2) Metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU), p50/p95/p99 latencies per token and per-request, GPU utilization, host CPU, memory, NVLINK bandwidth, sequence length distribution, and batching stats.
3) Regression detection: baseline store for each topology, automated comparison with thresholded regressions (configurable % degrade or absolute p95 increase).
4) CI integration: daily runs on dedicated infra and on-push smoke runs that gate runtime PRs when regressions exceed thresholds.
5) Reporting: per-run artifact (JSON), Grafana dashboard snapshot link, and a regression digest emailed to stakeholders with top regression vectors.

Design notes:
- Use the existing perf-agent to spawn driver containers on each node and a coordinator to collect traces. Replace flaky internal time-sync calls with NTP-based sync and monotonic timers.
- For metric store use ClickHouse for aggregated token/time series and Prometheus pushgateway for scraped p95 histograms. Export raw traces to S3 for deep-dive.
- Harness should include a noise rejection step (outlier removal using median absolute deviation) and compute the 95th percentile from cleaned data to reduce transient spikes.

Deliverables:
- Benchmark harness repo with test definitions and topology templates.
- Baseline artifact bundle for each topology (JSON + metrics + dashboard).
- CI job definitions and PR gating rules.
- Runbook describing how to add a new GPU type or model size and how to interpret regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- The suite runs end-to-end on heterogeneous 4-node and 8-node clusters and produces stable p95 numbers across 3 repeated runs (variance < 8%).
- A regression detected by the suite produces a human-readable digest and blocks a runtime release candidate when configured as a gate.
- Dashboards populate automatically and artifacts are retained in S3 for 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks execute on 4-node and 8-node heterogeneous clusters and produce tokens/sec and p95 artifacts
Automated regression detection compares current run to stored baseline and flags >5% p95 regressions
Daily baseline runs succeed and CI smoke runs complete under 45 minutes
Artifacts (raw metrics, cleaned summaries, and dashboard snapshots) are uploaded to S3 and linked in run JSON

notes: Avoid synthetic single-GPU microbenchmarks — the goal is system-level behavior under TP/PP mixing and NVLINK saturation patterns.
Keep model weights in customer-oblivious public S3 buckets; use small sample datasets for reproducibility.
Schedule a 1-hour demo with runtime, infra, and PM when baseline artifacts are available.
